study_type_evidence.quote: Peptide stabilities were evaluated in blood ex vivo, serum obtained from the same animal, and commercial serum and plasma after an incubation period of one hour.
blood (200 to 300 μL) was collected via cardiac puncture to obtain a peptide concentration of approximately 31,5 μmol/L
We confirmed this assumption by comparing the proteolytic cleavage of Api88 and Api137 by human α-thrombin, which possesses the same Pro-Arg substrate specificity

ex_vivo_detail: Mouse. Female outbred CD-1 (Swiss) mice, 14-16 weeks, 28-40 g (Janvier Labs), were euthanized by carbon dioxide inhalation and terminally bled by cardiac puncture. The peptide solution was pre-loaded into the syringe so that blood mixed with peptide on collection, giving a fresh-blood ex vivo degradation assay at 37 C. Six matrices were compared: fresh blood (B), direct serum (DS) and activated serum (AS) from the same animals, plus commercial pooled mouse serum (PAA Laboratories) and commercial pooled CD-1 mouse K2EDTA plasma and lithium heparin plasma (Innovative Research). No peptide was administered to a living animal in this study.
in_vitro_detail: Purified human alpha-thrombin digestion of Api88, Api137 and LVPR-Onc112 to test the proposed thrombin cleavage sites (S3 Fig and S1 Text). Peptide synthesis, purification by RPC and characterisation by analytical HPLC and MALDI-TOF/TOF-MS.

concentration_time_figure.caption_quote: Peptides in blood (dark red), direct serum (red), activated serum (orange), commercial serum (yellow), heparin plasma (dark blue), and EDTA plasma (blue) were analyzed after 10 min (Api88) and one hour (Api134 and Api137) incubation.
concentration_time_figure.note: Figs 2, 3 and 4 plot %-remaining peptide by MATRIX at a single endpoint (60 min, or 10 min for Api88), not against time, so they are not concentration-time curves. Fig 1 plots fibrinopeptide A and its metabolite peak areas at two time points (0 h and 1 h) per matrix, but that is a coagulation marker, not one of the test peptides. Api88 was additionally sampled at 1, 10 and 30 min and those percentages are given in the Results text, but no figure plots them against time.

bioanalytical_method: RP-HPLC with UV detection at 214 nm (Jupiter C18) for quantification of intact peptide relative to time zero; LC coupled on-line to electrospray-ionization ion-trap MS (Agilent 1100 / Bruker Esquire HCT) for metabolite identification and quantification; MALDI-TOF/TOF-MS for monoisotopic mass confirmation of synthesized peptides
bioanalytical_quote: Samples were analyzed by RP-HPLC on a Jupiter C18-column ... Peptides were detected by recording the absorbance at 214 nm and quantified by their peak areas relative to the initial peak areas (0 min).
notes: This study contains NO in vivo dosing. Mice were euthanized and terminally bled by cardiac puncture into a syringe that already contained the peptide solution, so all peptide exposure is ex vivo. in_vivo_species is therefore an empty array. The PeplLife2 metadata labels these rows 'In Vitro'; per the protocol's definition, blood/serum/plasma degradation assays are ex vivo (the human alpha-thrombin digestion in S3 Fig is the only genuinely in vitro exposure). None of the eight peptides had a half-life measured in this study; the qualitative PeplLife2 descriptors (Highly/Medium/Low Stable) correspond to Table 3 'Stability of eight peptides in fresh blood, serum, and plasma' (High: Api134/Api137/Onc112; Medium: Onc18/Onc72; Low: Api88/AAYR-Onc112/LVPR-Onc112). The numeric half-lives quoted in the body (Api88 <5 min, Api134 4 h, Api137 6 h, Onc18 20 min in Results but 25 min in Discussion, Onc72 3 h, Onc112 >8 h, all in mouse serum) are explicitly attributed to earlier publications, not measured here; note the internal 20 vs 25 min discrepancy for Onc18. The statement that 'Onc112 exhibited an improved pharmacokinetic profile and around fivefold higher plasma levels than Onc72 after intravenous application in mice' is likewise cited prior work. Peptide concentration in every matrix was ~31.5 umol/L; blood volume drawn into the peptide syringe was 200-300 uL. Sampling: 1 and 60 min in blood (1, 10 and 30 min for Api88); 0 and 60 min in serum/plasma (0, 10 and 30 min for Api88). Replication: 'at least in triplicates' for stability tests, and 'Six to nine samples were analyzed for each matrix' for the fibrinopeptide A analysis. Api137 was used as an internal 100%-stability reference to bound a ~10% matrix-effect error in the blood samples.
